rationale: Both candidates correctly recognize that the diff already fixes the GT's partition-gating, offline-example, and both inline (packed_total/attn_backend) issues, and both independently rediscover the one concern still live at this snapshot — the engine's async_omni_engine.py silently forcing rel_l1_thresh=0.2 and defeating the new 0.17 MiniMax-H3 default — with strong file:line evidence. Y edges ahead on precision and actionability: it demonstrates the engine bug via actual executed I/O traces, adds a genuinely novel and technically deep finding (the calibration polynomial is near-constant/non-monotone over its own domain), and organizes findings into clearly prioritized blocking/should-fix/minor tiers with a dedicated 'verified correct' section that reduces ambiguity. X is comparably thorough (notably the Cache-DiT/quality='high' conflict and AMD CI-relevance catch are valuable, well-hedged findings) but is slightly more mechanically listed and its extra findings skew more cosmetic.
